post_clip.description: Two individuals engage in mutual physical confrontation near the doorway: one person (in dark clothing) enters and immediately confronts the standing individual; both adopt aggressive postures, with visible pushing/shoving and rapid movement consistent with fighting. The interaction escalates quickly from entry to close-contact struggle, satisfying the definition of mutual combat.

A man in dark clothing is seen repeatedly bending over and striking the lower part of a glass door frame or threshold with his hands/arms (frames 3–5), suggesting deliberate forceful impact—consistent with attempted forced entry or vandalism. The motion is aggressive and repetitive, not accidental. No second person is visible, so it does not meet the 'fighting' definition, but it qualifies as suspicious criminal activity (burglary attempt or property damage).
